sources.fact: Newcastle University (Jan 9, 2013): wrinkled fingers give a better grip in wet conditions; wrinkling is an active process caused by blood vessels constricting below the skin, controlled by the autonomic nervous system; volunteers were 12% faster with wet marbles when their fingers were wrinkled; wrinkles make no difference for moving dry objects; could be working like treads on car tyres

Nature News (2013): people often assume wrinkling is water passing into the outer skin; researchers have known since the 1930s that the effect does not occur when there is nerve damage in the fingers; it is an involuntary reaction of the autonomic nervous system; wrinkles channel away water like rain treads in car tyres

post.instagram_caption:
Your wrinkly bath fingers might be tyre treads 🛁

Pruney fingers aren't just water soaking in. Your nervous system squeezes the blood vessels under your fingertips on purpose, which is why fingers with damaged nerves don't wrinkle. In a 2013 Newcastle University study, people moved wet marbles 12% faster with wrinkly fingers, and dry marbles made no difference.

The idea: the wrinkles channel water away, like treads on a car tyre.

Sources: Newcastle University, Nature.
